summary:
The Swanson and Hugh Butler Reservoirs Land Conveyances Act authorizes and directs a negotiated transfer of specified Bureau of Reclamation lands and waters at Swanson Reservoir and Hugh Butler Reservoir in Nebraska to Hitchcock County or Frontier County, as applicable, through title transfer agreements, rather than by amendment to the United States Code.

Section 2 defines the covered “requested Federal land” to include, in whole or subset as covered by a title transfer agreement, the Lakeview Lodge Permitted Concession Land, Red Willow Permitted Cabin Land, Red Willow Permitted Concession Land, Swanson Permitted Cabin Land, and Swanson Permitted Concession Land. It also defines the relevant reservoirs as Pick-Sloan Missouri Basin Program, Frenchman-Cambridge Division facilities authorized by section 9 of the Flood Control Act of 1944.

Section 3(a) requires the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Commissioner of Reclamation, subject to sections 4 and 5, to make good-faith efforts, not later than three years after enactment, to negotiate and enter into title transfer agreements with Hitchcock County and Frontier County. Each agreement must provide for conveyance of all requested United States right, title, and interest in the applicable requested Federal land, require that the land be conveyed in whole and not subdivided, and include a plan demonstrating the county’s permanent technical capability and financial ability to operate and maintain the land and to address State fire, safety, and health code compliance within two years after conveyance. Notwithstanding 43 U.S.C. 2902(3)(B), the agreements must be negotiated under the criteria, terms, and conditions of subtitle A of title VIII of the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act, 43 U.S.C. 2901 et seq. After execution, the Secretary must offer conveyance in accordance with the agreement.

As consideration, the county must pay fair market value as determined by a Secretary-approved third-party appraisal under USPAP, excluding permit-holder improvements and considering specified future federal revenue streams; disputes are resolved under 43 C.F.R. 2201.4. Proceeds are available to the Secretary, subject to further appropriation, for operation of Hugh Butler and Swanson Reservoirs. The county must also pay necessary survey and administrative conveyance costs in advance. Conveyed lands must be managed for substantially the same existing purposes or for specified recreation, public access, habitat, or natural-character purposes. Subsequent reconveyance is prohibited except to specified Nebraska public or governmental entities at no cost upon stated findings, and future conveyances remain subject to the Act’s management restrictions.

Section 4 makes conveyances subject to valid existing rights, Pick-Sloan operational requirements, reserved flowage easements, applicable management-agreement reservations, mineral rights and recorded permits or rights as of enactment, elevation-based deed restrictions on new permanent structures, and access easements. It limits federal liability, requires indemnification and hold-harmless agreements, preserves Federal Tort Claims Act limits, and provides that temporary flooding or flood damage is not a taking. Section 5 keeps the identified management agreements and applicable permits in force until the later of three years after enactment or conveyance, and requires continued federal management under applicable law for lands not covered by a title transfer agreement by that deadline.
